questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests understanding of fine-grained RBAC in Azure AD using Administrative Units to scope admin permissions, a common real-world need.

## Key Concepts

- Administrative Units scope admin permissions to a subset of objects
- RBAC role assignments with scope to an AU
- Validation through attempted cross-AU actions
- Simple rollback by removing scope and role assignments

## Code Example

```bash
# Create Marketing AU
az ad administrative-unit create --display-name Marketing
# Create Marketing Admins group
az ad group create --display-name MarketingAdmins --mail-nickname MarketingAdmins
# Add admin to the group (example user_id)
az ad group member add --group MarketingAdmins --member-id <admin_user_id>
# Get AU object id and assign role scoped to AU
az ad lro administrative-unit show --id Marketing | jq -r '.id'
az role assignment create --assignee <admin_user_id> --role "User Administrator" --scope <AU_id>
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle auditing to prove the scope remains restricted? 
- What failure modes might require re-scoping or a rollback plan?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates real-world multi-tenant Azure AD OIDC integration with Vault, emphasizing least privilege, credential revocation, and operational automation.

## Key Concepts
- Azure AD OIDC with a multi-tenant app registration
- Vault auth/oidc method with bound_claims for tenant-to-role mapping
- Namespaces and per-tenant policies for tenant isolation
- Token TTLs, rotation, and automated credential revocation

## Code Example
```hcl
# Vault OIDC role example per tenant
vault write auth/oidc/role/tenant-<tid> \
  bound_audiences="<AAD-Client-Id>" \
  bound_claims={"tid":"<tenant-id>"} \
  user_claim="upn" \
  token_ttl="1h" \
  token_max_ttl="24h" \
  token_policies=["tenant-<tid>-policy"]

# Namespace-scoped policy example
path "namespace/<tenant-id>/*" {
  capabilities = ["read", "list"]
}
```

## Design Considerations
| Concern | Recommendation |
|---------|----------------|
| Tenant isolation | Separate namespaces with dedicated policies |
| Token lifetime | 15–60 min TTL, 24h max TTL with renewal |
| Rapid revocation | Vault token revoke + Azure AD token invalidation |
| Compromised tenant | Conditional access policies + batch token revocation |
| Sandbox validation | Pre-deployment testing in isolated namespace |
| Rollback | Immediate token revocation + access policy deny-all |
